[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Time-Series Database Design: A Technical Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Time-series databases (TSDBs) are specialized data management systems optimized for handling timestamped data points or metrics. Designing an efficient TSDB schema requires understanding unique access patterns, high ingestion rates, and specific retention policies."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Characteristics of Time-Series Data"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"High Write Volume: Data arrives continuously from sensors, servers, or financial feeds."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Append-Only: Historical data is rarely updated; insertions overwhelmingly dominate over updates."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Time-Centric Queries: Queries typically aggregate data over specific time windows (e.g., average CPU usage over the last hour)."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Schema Design Principles"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"A well-designed time-series schema separates metadata (tags) from numerical measurements (fields). Tags are typically indexed for fast filtering, while fields store the raw metric values."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"CREATE TABLE server_metrics (
  time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  server_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  region TEXT NOT NULL,
  cpu_usage DOUBLE PRECISION,
  memory_usage DOUBLE PRECISION
);"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Partitioning and Data Retention"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because time-series data grows indefinitely, tables must be partitioned by time (e.g., daily or hourly chunks). This allows the database to drop old partitions instantly rather than executing expensive DELETE queries when enforcing retention policies."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"SELECT create_hypertable('server_metrics', 'time', chunk_time_interval => INTERVAL '1 day');"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Compression Strategies"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"TSDBs leverage columnar storage and specialized compression algorithms. Timestamps are compressed using delta-of-delta encoding, floating-point numbers use Gorilla compression, and repetitive string tags use dictionary encoding to drastically reduce disk footprints."}]
